input: Strings contain only ASCII characters U+0000 through U+007F, so Python code-point and JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit indexing agree. Arbitrary Unicode and boxed strings are outside the paired domain. s has length n with 0 <= n <= 134217727, ensuring the maximum substring count fits a safe integer. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The integer count of nonempty palindromic contiguous substring occurrences, counting equal text at different positions separately. Empty input returns 0. This is not a count of distinct palindrome values.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only scalar center, endpoint and count state is used; no substring or table is materialized.
numeric: The maximum result is n*(n + 1)/2 <= 9007199187632128 for n <= 134217727. The source accumulates by exact increments rather than multiplying those bounds at runtime. Endpoint increments and -1 sentinels remain safe. Python arbitrary-size integers do not broaden the paired length domain.
complexity: O(n*n + 1) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary space. For each character center, offset 0 expands odd palindromes and offset 1 expands even palindromes. Every palindromic interval has exactly one such center/offset and is counted once. Inputs of repeated identical characters attain quadratic work; no linear-time claim is made.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 412 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs.
